subject: gate-coverage
text:
- Child `viola` processes spawned by E2E tests are included, because `LLVM_PROFILE_FILE` propagates. Tests that call `env_clear()` must re-add it. The one deliberate exception is not the product: the harness self-tests' nested cargo over the throwaway `mini` crate (package `viola`) removes cargo-llvm-cov's four names (`CARGO_LLVM_COV`, `LLVM_PROFILE_FILE`, `RUSTC_WRAPPER`, `__CARGO_LLVM_COV_RUSTC_WRAPPER_RUSTFLAGS`) through `test_support::uninstrumented`, so the throwaway's binaries write no profile into the outer run — as measured at chunk 2026-09-29-h2-conpty-resize-probe on the dev host (new `.profraw` per run of one such self-test: 17 with the names inherited, 13 without, the throwaway's two binary signatures gone). That a corrupt-header profile failing the ubuntu merge (ci#36529038462, and ci#36481260151 before it) came through this channel is recorded, not established: the job log names no writer. One mechanism for such a profile is measured (as measured at chunk 2026-10-07-a-send-ending-in-a-newline-is-confirmed, `evidence/profraw-red-green.md`): an instrumented child that exits by itself and is killed during its exit-time profile write leaves a short profile, which `llvm-profdata` refuses. The root bin's `start_opens_the_scenario_one_spans_under_run_start` started its wrapper with the test binary itself; the wrapper puts its plugin flag first, libtest refuses it and exits 101 at once, and the test kills the child straight after the start. On the dev host 3 of 4 800 loaded runs left a third profile, all three short. The test's child is now the host program `whoami`, which is not instrumented and writes no profile whenever the kill lands: 4 800 loaded runs then left one whole profile each.
 The coverage-merge red of ci#37627485806 attempt 1 (`test (ubuntu-latest)`, on `9f2bebe`) is closed by this mechanism, with a limit: the refused profile's writer, pid 10799, is not provable from the run (`evidence/ci-attempt-1.md`). The two earlier runs above are not claimed closed. A second mechanism is measured: a test that kills the wrapper closes its PTY, and the hangup reaches the hooks the fake agent ran in that terminal's foreground process group, so a `viola hook` cut off in its exit-time profile write leaves a page-cut profile that `llvm-profdata` refuses, or none; with every command the fake agent spawns in a process group of its own (the fake agent's exit bullet, §7) the census over the kill-shaped `chaos_wait_parked_wrapper_killed_exits_21` reads 0 refused profiles of 800 in 200 runs (as measured at `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-20-epoch-5-cleanup/evidence/profraw-cause.md`). The witness is `scripts/profraw-census.sh <runs> <workers> [<name>]`, with a second form `--case <binary stem> <test name> <runs> <workers> [<name>]` over one integration case that offers each profile alone to `llvm-profdata merge` and counts the refused ones, a dev-host script (architecture §Occupied Resources → Repository): no CI job, `pre-push` stage or harness command runs it, and it has no unit test, only its recorded one-shot controls (must-fail on the untouched test, must-pass, and two planted readings).

subject: gate-mutation
text:
**Mutation gate (Founder Direction 1):** judged at the epoch boundary by `/andromeda-code-audit` and on demand by `run --mutants`; no chunk, pre-push or CI mutation gate exists since 2026-09-28 (the founder's ruling, 17:59). `mutants.out/outcomes.json` for the diff (the run's own output: under the host mutation scratch on a Windows host, §3 `run` step 4) must show `missed == 0`, `timeout == 0` and `unviable <= caught`, where `missed` reads after the harness has left out the host-excluded records (§3 `run` step 4, Verdict). `unviable` mutants are reported, and a few do not fail the gate. When they outnumber the caught ones the run is red (`unviable-exceeds-caught`), because a run whose mutant builds mostly failed is no evidence of test strength. The threshold was picked by measurement across every CI leg with an uploaded verdict while the legs existed (2026-09-25). Healthy legs had unviable/caught ≤ 0.044 (chunk 7: 3/114 and 3/113; this cleanup: 4/139, 4/139, and 6/137 on the dev host). The failed windows leg of run 36118112104 had 135/8. A diff that names no `.rs` path (docs, specs, fixtures) never reaches cargo-mutants: it passes with the explicit `"mutants":{"tested":0,"verdict":"no-rust-delta","diff":"target/agent-run/chunk.diff","files":N}`. A diff whose `.rs` paths are all test targets (`tests/`, `benches/`, `examples/`, at the root or under `crates/<member>/`) has nothing cargo-mutants can mutate: it passes only with the explicit `test-only-rust-delta` verdict, which names the diff, its file count and `rust_files`. Any other diff naming a `.rs` path, a mixed one included, is `counted`, and a counted run that produces no fresh `outcomes.json` is red. A mutant caught only by a doctest counts as missed under nextest, so the missing unit test must be added.
 The boundary tier scores a whole member with `run --mutants --package <member>` (viola-e2e: `run --mutants --package viola-e2e`, its verdict `package`) under the same `missed == 0`, `timeout == 0`, `unviable <= caught`. A mutant this host cannot compile or reach — inside a `cfg(windows)` item or block, or behind a const such as `HOST_SCRATCH = cfg!(windows)` — is recorded "not measured here; owed to {the route entry that measures it}" by coordinate, never "equivalent", and never counted as caught; `missed == 0` then reads over the measurable set (the overseer's ruling, 2026-10-04). Since chunk 2026-10-10-windows-mutation-grade the harness applies the first case itself: a missed mutant whose whole span sits under a `cfg` attribute proved false for the host is left out of the count and named with its predicate in the document's `mutants.host_excluded` (§3 `run` step 4, Verdict). A mutant behind a const compiles on both hosts, is never left out, and stays a record by coordinate. The first whole-member `viola-e2e` score on the Linux dev host read 718 mutants in 5356 s (89 min 16 s): 656 caught, 2 missed, 0 timeout, 60 unviable, as measured at `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-09-epoch-3-cleanup-ii/evidence/e2e-score.md`. Its 2 missed are in `prepare` (`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run/mutants/scratch.rs`). `prepare` takes its host flag from `mutate()` (`scratch::HOST_SCRATCH`), so both arms are reached on every host, and both mutants (`Ok(None)` and the deleted `!`) read killed on the Linux dev host by its scratch case (as measured at `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-20-epoch-5-cleanup-ii/evidence/survivors.ndjson`). The route entry "Windows mutation grade" measured them: both read caught on `windows-2025` (run 38036448183, job `mutants (viola-e2e)`).
 The Epoch 4 boundary audit's Linux whole-member runs read 47 missed (`.andromeda/runs/2026-10-12T06-54-29-code-audit/record.json`, `mutation.survivors`); chunk 2026-10-13-epoch-4-survivors disposed each in its ledger `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-13-epoch-4-survivors/evidence/survivors.ndjson`: 29 by a nextest case in the package that owns the mutated file, 7 of them after a behaviour-preserving restatement that made the site reachable on Linux (`viola_state::fs`'s retry decision passed in by the caller, `viola send`'s issue-line decision a named function), each shown red under its hand-applied mutant and green restored with no mutation run made; the 2 `prepare` rows above stood as recorded (killed on every host since, above); and the 16 in `src/cmd/verify/typed.rs` (whose code now sits under its children in `src/cmd/verify/typed/`; `framing_turns` 5, `SharedPty` 5, `Run`'s ending sequence 6) were disposed by chunk 2026-10-13-epoch-4-survivors-ii in its ledger `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-13-epoch-4-survivors-ii/evidence/survivors.ndjson`, each after a behaviour-preserving restatement inside that module (the two framing waits the named predicates `added_turn_ended` and `local_command_answered`, every `clock.now() + PROBE_DEADLINE` the one function `probe_until`, `SharedPty` generic over its `Pty` and reached through a test-only recording double, the Ctrl-C ending and the pump wait the plain functions `ctrl_c_ending` and `ended_by`) and a case in its unit tests, each shown red under its hand-applied mutant and green restored with no mutation run made; none is owed. The Epoch 5 boundary audit's own run is the reader that confirms the 45 kills (the 29 of chunk 2026-10-13-epoch-4-survivors and the 16 of chunk 2026-10-13-epoch-4-survivors-ii).
 The Epoch 5 boundary audit's 16 survivors were each disposed by a nextest case in the package that owns the mutated file, 10 killed and 6 after a behaviour-preserving restatement, each red under its hand-applied mutant and green reverted byte-exact, with no mutation run made and none equivalent or recorded (as measured at `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-20-epoch-5-cleanup-ii/evidence/survivors.ndjson`). The boundary audit measures the `cfg(windows)` code by dispatching `windows-mutants.yml` (founder ruling C2, 2026-10-04; §9 Mutation row): `run --mutants --package <member> --file …` per matrix item on `windows-2025` (§9 Mutation row), verdict `package`, report-only and never a gate. In its first run, 37174673472, 19 of 25 misses were `#[cfg(unix)]` twins in the scoped files, which the Windows build compiles out and cargo-mutants grades missed, with 0 timeouts across 508 mutants (`viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-04-windows-boundary-mutation-workflow/evidence/windows-dispatch.md`). The harness now leaves such twins out itself (§3 `run` step 4, Verdict). Run 38036448183 read all nine jobs green over 642 mutants: 537 caught, 75 unviable, 30 left out as host-excluded (the sum of the nine documents' `host_excluded` lengths), 0 missed and 0 timeout, the longest job 49 min against the 120 min ceiling, as measured at `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-10-windows-mutation-grade/evidence/windows-dispatch.md`. That run was one dispatch outside the boundary audit, made on 2026-10-10 for chunk 2026-10-10-windows-mutation-grade alone and on the founder's own word for it; the ruling stands as written.
 On the Linux dev host every mutation run takes `TMPDIR=<repo parent>/viola-mutants-scratch`, a NOCOW (`chattr +C`) btrfs dir set by the operator (an environment fact; the harness's scratch arm stays Windows-only): cargo-mutants 27.1.0 copies the tree, `target/` included, into the temp dir; `/tmp` there is a 32 GB `usrquota` tmpfs that a full viola-e2e run overflowed at 460/709; and on a COW btrfs dir its reflink copy drops the exec bit of the prebuilt `viola-fake-agent` (as measured at `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-03-mutation-scoring-completion/evidence/m3.md`). The Epoch 4 audit ran two cargo-mutants jobs (`-j 2`) under one such `TMPDIR` and read viola-pty's `PortablePty::resize` → `Ok(())` missed, while its three resize tests, run alone under that mutant, read red (as measured at chunk 2026-10-13-epoch-4-survivors, `evidence/survivors.md`); that the other job's unmutated run wrote the awaited `size 120x40` line into the report file both shared is recorded, not established (the two-job run was not re-run). The report files now carry the test process's id (architecture §Occupied Resources), so two jobs never share one. The two real-cargo-mutants harness tests (`run_mutants_passes_when_the_change_is_tested`, `run_mutants_reports_survivors_of_an_untested_change`) are compiled out on macOS (`#[cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))]`, never `#[ignore]`): there cargo-mutants' baseline build in its copied tree takes ~77 s of an 80.9 s phase against 0.41 s for the same cold build outside it, with no first-launch or jobserver cost, as measured at CI run 36481260151 (the chunk 2026-09-28-mutation-testing-to-the-epoch-boundary's `evidence/macos-mutants-phases.md`); the cause inside that phase stays unnamed, so under the operator's ruling it is runner-side. Both run on ubuntu and windows; `[profile.ci]`'s 120 s kill and `retries = 0` are unchanged.

subject: gate-perf
text:
- **Perf session:** `--perf` then boots ONE session through its `PerfSession` seam (`boot::boot` / `cleanup::cleanup`; the harness's own tests stand in for both): `perf-<harness pid>`, a `builder` instance, `BootOptions { bin_dir: target/perf/release, build: false, stamp: false }`, its home under `target/e2e-home/` (boot step 2), unstamped, so the `pre-tool-use` row times the unverified-CLI path (`hook.dialog` → `null` at once). Each row's synthetic payload (string fields only, the tests-owned content canary in content fields; no recorded fixture exists yet) is written to `target/agent-run/<session>/payload-<hook>.json` and fed through `--input`; hyperfine runs with the repo root as cwd and `VIOLA_NAME=builder` / `VIOLA_DIR=<perf home>/instances/builder` set, so every timed hook takes the real logging and channel path, never the no-instance no-op (obs-plan §10 obs-overhead row) — as measured at chunk 2026-09-28-hook-perf-gate: a kept-home run held 132 `hook-decision` lines with no fallback `detail` and 33 wrapper events per row. Each row's stale export is removed first. After the last row and **before** `cleanup`, `--perf` asserts the home's role files (`diagnostics/*.ndjson` without `detail-*`) hold no `event:"panic"` line, with no seam exemption, because a hook panic exits 0 and hyperfine cannot see it; a panic line fails `panic`. Then `cleanup` (`keep_homes` = `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES` exactly `1`) must report `ok:true`. A failed build (`build`), boot (`boot: <reason>`), row (the hook's name), panic check or cleanup turns suite `perf` red with the failure named, never a missing or skipped row.
 Every timed hook also runs its instance strict-modes check (`check_instance`) before any `config.json` read or obs init, and makes its server check (the peer pid and its OS start time against the one snapshot read) before its first frame; with both checks in the timed path the five hook rows read `max` 2.5 / 2.4 / 2.4 / 2.4 / 3.3 ms on the Linux dev host, under `SPINE_DEADLINE`, as measured at `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-26-home-and-code-bearing-file-integrity/report.md` (Outcome, `run --perf`).
